findings.summary: Brisling has lower median latency (41 ms) than Talmar (118 ms) on the Brindle-Voice test set, but the comparison is confounded by different hardware and precision (Brisling on Corvex A2 fp16, Talmar on Corvex A1 fp32).
findings.scope: Brindle-Voice test set, batch size 1, median latency per utterance
findings.caveats: Latency measured on different accelerators and precisions; Talmar latency copied from original paper, not re-measured.

findings.summary: Brisling uses 4.0 decoder passes per utterance versus Talmar's 37.6 passes, indicating a large reduction in decoding steps.
findings.scope: Brindle-Voice test set, decoder passes per utterance
findings.caveats: Passes are averaged over the test set; no statistical test reported.

findings.summary: Brisling's WER (6.4%) is slightly higher than Talmar's (6.1%) on the Brindle-Voice test set, a difference of 0.3 percentage points; no statistical test was reported, so this difference is not established as significant.
findings.caveats: No statistical test reported; difference may not be reliable.

findings.summary: Brisling has higher WER (6.4%) than Greedy-CTC (8.9%) but lower latency (41 ms vs 22 ms), showing a trade-off between accuracy and speed.
findings.scope: Brindle-Voice test set, WER (%) and median latency (ms)
findings.caveats: No statistical test reported; latency measured on same hardware for both.

Brisling required only 4.0 decoder passes per utterance compared to Talmar's 37.6, indicating a large reduction in decoding steps. Brisling's WER was 6.4%, slightly higher than Talmar's 6.1%, a difference of 0.3 percentage points, but no statistical test was reported, so this difference is not established as significant. Compared to Greedy-CTC, Brisling achieved a lower WER (6.4% vs 8.9%) but higher median latency (41 ms vs 22 ms), reflecting a trade-off between accuracy and speed.
